subject: Private deployment responsibilities & temporary SLO waiver request
messages:
From: Alexandra Cho <alexandra.cho@sunrise-medtech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sunrise-medtech.com, techops@sunrise-medtech.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment responsibilities and temporary SLO waiver request

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for stepping through the private/VPC onboarding checklist with our infra team this week. We are planning the final cutover for the Redwood Private deployment on 2026-12-05. A couple of operational items came up that we need Redwood's support on before we go live:

1) Customer-controlled edge routing: Sunrise will manage the colo/router, BGP peers, and our NAT translation. We expect asymmetric routing and transient jitter during the initial 2–3 week peering stabilization window.
2) Observability handoff: We can provide NetFlow and aggregated telemetry but cannot provide host-level agent access into our edge routers due to compliance constraints.
3) Evidence for SLO attribution: Procurement needs a written acceptance criteria that will be used to decide whether incidents are classified as 'Customer-controlled network' vs. Redwood responsibility.

Given the above, procurement is asking Redwood to accept a temporary, limited SLO waiver for network-attributed latency/availability impacts during the migration period (proposed 90 days) or until the stabilization evidence is accepted. We’re attaching the current network diagram and will produce a runbook + test plan by next week.

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood needs to accept an exception (packet captures, NetFlow ranges, jitter thresholds, scheduled maintenance windows), and whether Redwood can propose specific amendment language we can feed to legal?

Attachments: network-diagram_v2.pdf (network diagram)

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is targeting sign-off by 2026-11-29.

Best,
Alexandra Cho
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Sunrise MedTech
[Attachment: network-diagram_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Cho <alexandra.cho@sunrise-medtech.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment responsibilities and temporary SLO waiver request

Alexandra —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the diagram. High level: we can accommodate a time-boxed exception for customer-controlled network impacts, but we need a concrete evidence and acceptance plan before we amend any SLOs. Quick summary of what we require and the steps I recommend: 

- Evidence we need from Sunrise:
  * Signed runbook that lists maintenance windows, expected BGP peer IP ranges, and test traffic endpoints.
  * Aggregated NetFlow/flow logs with time-correlated spikes for any incident you claim is customer-attributable.
  * A short validation test (5–15 min) where Sunrise can trigger a controlled routing change and provide captures/NetFlow for verification.

- Proposed temporary scope & duration:
  * Scope: exclude customer-edge-attributable packet loss/jitter from Redwood's latency SLOs only when Sunrise provides the signed runbook and the post-incident flow logs.
  * Duration: Redwood proposes 60 days from cutover (we're flexible) or until the validation tests are completed and accepted — whichever is sooner.

- Controls we need to implement on our side:
  * A mutual action plan (MAP) doc to be attached as an appendix to the SLO amendment.
  * A telemetry acceptance checklist that legal & ops sign off on.

I’ve attached a lightweight mutual-action-plan-template you can use as a starting point. Can you confirm whether procurement/legal at Sunrise can accept the 60-day proposal, and whether the techops team can commit to a validation window the week after cutover? If so I’ll loop in our legal to draft the amending language (short, point-form).

Cc’ing Priyom (accounts) and Naomi (infra evidence) to start the internal review.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-template.docx (docx)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment responsibilities and temporary SLO waiver request

Team —

Looping you in for action items and quick decisions. Key asks from Sunrise: runbook, NetFlow evidence, and a validation test. Here’s what we need internally to move fast: 

- Naomi: please review the attached network diagram and the proposed evidence list. Can you confirm whether aggregated NetFlow (no packet-level host access) is sufficient for attribution? If not, what minimum additional telemetry do we need?
- Priyom: procurement wants a duration; I’ve proposed 60 days. If Sunrise pushes back to 90, can we counter with an operational milestone schedule instead of pure time (e.g., 60 days + two successful validation tests)?
- Karthik: ops/serving runtime — confirm fallback model variant behavior if we detect persistent latency not attributable to the customer. We should define automatic fallback to a smaller model or degraded throughput so their app remains responsive.

We want to avoid broad indemnity language or an open-ended waiver. If legal asks, I’ll draft a tight amendment that: (a) enumerates types of customer-controlled incidents; (b) requires the customer to provide flow evidence within 48 hours of an incident; (c) reassigns attribution to Redwood only if evidence is insufficient.

Please reply with quick yes/no on the telemetry ask and any redlines you foresee.

— Sean

From: Alexandra Cho <alexandra.cho@sunrise-medtech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sunrise-medtech.com, techops@sunrise-medtech.com
Date: 2026-11-21T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment responsibilities and temporary SLO waiver request

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM PDT, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alexandra —
> 
> Thanks for the clear write-up and the diagram. High level: we can accommodate a time-boxed exception for customer-controlled network impacts...

Thanks Sean — appreciate the practical path. Procurement is happy to accept a 60-day default with a 30-day extension option if the validation tests reveal additional stabilization work. We can commit to: 

- Providing the signed runbook and the first set of aggregated NetFlow logs within 48 hours of cutover.
- Scheduling a 10-minute controlled BGP flapping test (pre-approved maintenance window) for verification within the first 10 calendar days after cutover.
- Delivering packet-level captures only for the short controlled test (we cannot provide continuous packet capture).

We attach the preliminary runbook and the edge test plan for your review. If Redwood provides the proposed amendment language, we’ll share it with our legal and get procurement sign-off by 2026-11-29 as requested.

Our ask: an explicit acceptance checklist (bullet list) that your team will use to close the exception. Can Redwood confirm the acceptance criteria and the data formats you accept for NetFlow/flows?

Thanks — I’ll have techops stand by for the validation scheduling.

Best,
Alexandra Cho
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Sunrise MedTech
[Attachment: edge-runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)]
